$comment: The written catalogue of BSD/GNU-divergent shell invocations this repository refuses.
It is a DATA file and not a table inside the checker on purpose: what a gate
enforces has to be readable by someone who is not reading its code, and this
repository has already been bitten once by a limit that existed only inside an
implementation. What does not appear in this file passes in silence, so the
out_of_scope block below says out loud which divergences are NOT checked.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Measured on CI 2026-09-02: gate-lockfile-coherence.selftest.sh
was 16/16 on macOS and 11/16 on Linux. The five broken cases all used `sed -i ''`,
which is BSD syntax; GNU sed reads the empty string as the script and the mutation
never applies. The logic was right, the spelling was not portable, and the author's
green Mac said nothing about it.
FIELDS.
id          stable name, used in findings and in the written exemption comment
why         the divergence in one sentence: what breaks, on which platform
portable    the spelling that works on both, when one exists
pattern     Python regex; a match on a logical line is a candidate
counterpart Python regex for the OTHER platform's spelling of the same command.
A candidate is exonerated when the same logical line ALSO matches
this and contains `||` - the deliberate fallback idiom
`A 2>/dev/null || B`. null means no such pair exists and the only
way out is the written exemption.
Measured before writing: over 104 shell files under scripts/, a catalogue with no
counterpart logic flagged 18 CORRECT lines - 16 mktemp fallbacks and one date
fallback pair. A gate whose first red is its own defect gets switched off, so the
fallback idiom is recognised rather than punished.
out_of_scope: Shell built-ins whose behaviour differs between bash and dash (`local`, `echo`);
this repository pins `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, and a shebang gate is a different check.
Anything outside scripts/ - .github/workflows/ is covered by gate-actions-lint.sh.
awk dialects (mawk/gawk/BSD awk) and their `--posix` divergences: real, but the
repository carries no awk invocation that depends on one, so a rule for it would
be a rule nobody can test in the negative here.
`ls` output parsing, `head -c`/`tail -c` on non-seekable input, and locale-driven
`sort` collation: not lexically decidable from a single line.

Whether the counterpart spelling that exonerates a line is really its fallback. The test is lexical: counterpart present on the same logical line, plus an `||`. An unrelated `grep -E` beside a genuinely lone `grep -P` therefore exonerates it. Telling those apart means parsing the shell, so this is a known false negative and not an oversight.

rules.why: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS; GNU sed reads the empty string as the script and edits nothing.
rules.portable: edit with python3, or write to a temp file and mv it into place

rules.why: `sed -i` with no suffix is GNU; BSD sed consumes the next argument as the backup suffix.
rules.portable: edit with python3, or write to a temp file and mv it into place
sed -E, understood by both since macOS 10.7

rules.why: `stat -f FMT` is BSD; on GNU `-f` selects a file system, not a format.
rules.portable: read the field with python3 os.stat, or wc -c for a size

rules.why: `stat -c FMT` is GNU; BSD spells the same thing `-f`.
rules.portable: read the field with python3 os.stat, or wc -c for a size
compute the instant in python3 and format it there
compute the instant in python3 and format it there

rules.why: `readlink -f` is absent on macOS before 12.3 and on older BSD.
`mktemp -t X` takes a PREFIX on BSD and a TEMPLATE on GNU; the resulting names differ.
rules.portable: mktemp -d, with the -t form only as an explicit `||` fallback

rules.why: `grep -P` needs PCRE, which BSD grep does not carry.
rules.portable: grep -E, or match with python3 re

rules.why: `xargs -r` is GNU; BSD xargs already skips an empty input and rejects the flag.
rules.portable: guard the pipeline with `[ -s file ]` instead

rules.why: `find -perm +NNN` is BSD; GNU removed it in favour of `/NNN` and errors out.
`base64 -w` is GNU line wrapping; BSD spells it `-b` and errors on `-w`.

rules.portable: mkdir -p on the destination directory, then cp

rules.why: `tar --wildcards` is GNU tar; bsdtar matches patterns without it and rejects the flag.
rules.portable: extract everything and filter afterwards, or pass explicit member names

rules.why: `sort -V` is GNU version sort; BSD sort gained it late and older macOS lacks it.
`echo -e` is not POSIX; whether it interprets escapes or prints `-e` depends on the shell.
